stage: Stage 0A - prior-art closure and formal problem freeze

claims.statement: No scholarly full text could be obtained in this environment, including author-hosted and institutional copies.
claims.evidence: WebFetch on arxiv.org returned EGRESS_BLOCKED this stage. Direct probes of isas.iar.kit.edu, ivan.ece.ufl.edu, shemesh.larc.nasa.gov, csl.sri.com, doi.org, citeseerx, researchgate and docs.px4.io all returned 000. Recorded in REQUIRED_READING_MANIFEST.md section 0.
claims.assumptions: The probes reflect session egress policy rather than transient failure. Two independent mechanisms (WebFetch and curl) agree.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Zero full texts were read; the prior-art gate of item 1 could not be executed.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: The prior art was audited. / We reviewed the closest papers.
claims.next_falsification_test: Re-probe on a machine with library access; the claim is environment-specific.

claims.statement: The evidence-provenance topology of ArduPilot changes during flight: the VIBRATION message follows _first_usable_accel, which is reassigned every main-loop iteration from sensor health.
claims.evidence: GCS_Common.cpp:3075 calls ins.get_vibration_levels(); AP_InertialSensor.h:312 resolves it to get_vibration_levels(_first_usable_accel); AP_InertialSensor.cpp:2001-2006 reassigns the index inside update() (function opens at 1926) from _accel_healthy[], which is cleared at 1986-1989. ArduPilot 01a504b, the revision csia/aircraft/adapters/ardupilot.py:3 already declares itself verified against.
claims.assumptions: The overload resolution is as read; no later override reassigns the index. Only three message families were audited.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: In ArduPilot 01a504b the accelerometer instance behind the VIBRATION message is selected at runtime from sensor health, and the wire message carries no field identifying it (common.xml:6632-6641).
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Nobody knows which accelerometer VIBRATION comes from. / This is an undiscovered defect.
claims.next_falsification_test: Replay a log in which an accel is failed and confirm the vibration series discontinuity - not run in this stage.

claims.statement: PX4 already represents the same phenomenon as a first-class message, which reframes the ArduPilot finding as a telemetry gap in one stack rather than a conceptual gap in the field.
claims.evidence: msg/SensorSelection.msg carries accel_device_id and gyro_device_id and its own comment says it is updated when sensor selection changes; published at src/modules/sensors/voted_sensors_update.cpp:276; consumed to follow the switch at VehicleAngularVelocity.cpp:81-82.
claims.assumptions: That publication on change means downstream consumers can observe it. Whether PX4 forwards it over MAVLink was not checked.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: One of the two autopilot stacks audited already publishes the selection identity on change; what ArduPilot lacks is a field on the wire, not the concept.
claims.next_falsification_test: Check whether any MAVLink message forwards SensorSelection from PX4; if none does, the telemetry gap is common to both stacks.

claims.statement: The frontier report's claim that kappa = 1 implies the consistency residual has zero power against a fault at the cut vertex is false as stated.
claims.evidence: MENGER_CLAIM_COUNTEREXAMPLES.md section 1: with y1 = f1(c), y2 = f2(c), the residual r = y1 - y2 has dr/ddelta = f1'(c) - f2'(c), non-zero whenever f1' differs from f2'. Instantiated on the audited pair: vibration.rms is a high-passed magnitude statistic and imu1.accel a low-passed signed vector, so a step bias at the shared accelerometer moves one and not the other.
claims.assumptions: Differentiability where used; the finite-difference version carries the same argument.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Shared provenance does not imply diagnostic blindness. Blindness requires residual invariance at the cut vertex, which is a condition on the functional forms and not on the graph.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: The residual is always sensitive. / The frontier report was worthless.
claims.next_falsification_test: None needed; the counterexample is constructive.

claims.statement: Item 11's hostile null H_KILL_PROVENANCE holds in both directions, so kappa_prov is not sufficient as the central quantity.
claims.evidence: MENGER_CLAIM_COUNTEREXAMPLES.md section 1 proves the first clause (same source, distinct constraints, residual still sensitive); section 3 proves the second (distinct sources, shared physical disturbance, residual blind, no software edge to draw).
claims.assumptions: That physical common-mode coupling between co-located transducers is real. This is standard engineering knowledge, not a measurement made here.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: A source-provenance graph alone can neither certify nor refute diagnostic information diversity. kappa_prov is at most a screening heuristic with known false positives and false negatives.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Provenance is useless. / kappa_prov has been redefined so that it works.
claims.next_falsification_test: Exhibit a class of systems in which both counterexample directions are excluded by construction; none is known.

claims.statement: The bound direction asserted in the frontier report is wrong: omitted edges make kappa_prov an under-estimate, not an over-estimate, and no single bound direction holds in general.
claims.evidence: FORMAL_REDUCTION.md section 4. Removing edges cannot create paths, so by Menger the min cut of a subgraph is <= that of the true graph; worked case {s1->a, s1->b, s2->b} with s2->b omitted gives 1 < 2. Aliasing (modelling one physical object as two nodes) runs the other way. research/frontier_selection/SELECTED_CANDIDATE_FORMAL_TARGET.md section 6 PO-2 asserts the opposite and is superseded.
claims.assumptions: The audit error taxonomy is exhaustive enough for the two directions shown; other error modes may exist.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: kappa_prov is a lower bound only under a no-aliasing assumption and an upper bound only under a no-omission assumption; a source audit discharges neither.
claims.next_falsification_test: None needed; the derivation is constructive. Note the practical consequence: an incomplete audit produces FALSE deficits, the direction that flatters the hypothesis.

claims.statement: The only formal statement item 9 permits is close to tautological, and graph structure cannot certify the invariance it needs.
claims.evidence: FORMAL_REDUCTION.md section 3. The permitted statement restates its own hypothesis. Counterexamples A and B show graph structure is consistent with both blindness and sensitivity, in both directions, so it is neither necessary nor sufficient for invariance.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: No non-trivial formal result relating graph separation to fault sensitivity was obtained, and the counterexamples indicate none of the proposed form exists.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: We prove a theorem about evidence structure.
claims.next_falsification_test: Find additional structural conditions under which certification becomes possible; none was found here.

claims.statement: The re-centring forced by the counterexamples moves the candidate onto structural FDI's own ground, worsening its prior-art position.
claims.evidence: FORMAL_REDUCTION.md section 5 concludes the only defensible quantity is residual fault sensitivity S_{R,f}. META_DIAGNOSIS_REDUCTION.md section 3 records that fault sensitivity of residuals is structural FDI's core apparatus and that meta-diagnosis asks whether the relation in use is sound.
claims.assumptions: Characterisation of structural FDI and meta-diagnosis from general background knowledge, NOT from full text. This is exactly why the stage cannot conclude.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: After the re-centring, the nearest prior art is closer than it was, and the P4 reduction is now the most serious of the four.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Meta-diagnosis subsumes candidate B. / Meta-diagnosis does not subsume candidate B.

claims.statement: Candidate B is not approved for Stage 0B.
claims.evidence: Item 1's gate returned INCONCLUSIVE_MISSING_FULLTEXT (REQUIRED_READING_MANIFEST.md section 2). Item 11's null holds (E5). Item 31 permits STAGE0B files only if every gate passes; two did not, so no Stage 0B artifacts were written.
claims.strongest_allowed_wording: Stage 0B is not authorised. The candidate is neither killed nor cleared; the prior-art question is unanswered and the central metric is insufficient as formulated.
claims.forbidden_stronger_wording: Candidate B is dead. / Candidate B is ready to test.
claims.next_falsification_test: Execute REQUIRED_READING_MANIFEST.md on a machine with library access, then re-run this stage.

refuted_predictions.prediction: Frontier stage R0.2 predicted that kappa_prov could serve as the central quantity for candidate B, under the name 'effective independence'.
refuted_predictions.outcome: Refuted. The name asserted a relationship to failure and statistical independence that is false in both directions, and the quantity neither measures nor certifies diagnostic diversity. Renamed to kappa_prov / structural evidence diversity per item 5, and demoted to a screening heuristic at best.
refuted_predictions.why_kept: It is the main result of this stage.

refuted_predictions.prediction: Frontier stage R0.2 asserted that kappa is an upper bound on effective independence, so 'a deficit found under an upper bound is real'.
refuted_predictions.outcome: Refuted. Omitted edges deflate kappa_prov, so an incomplete audit manufactures deficits that do not exist - the opposite direction, and the one that flatters the hypothesis. See E6.
refuted_predictions.why_kept: An error in the direction that would have made a false finding look conservative. It must stay visible.

refuted_predictions.prediction: Frontier stage R0.2 ranked the fusion literature (S063, S060) as the most dangerous prior art and ARP4761 as the single most likely cause of death.
refuted_predictions.outcome: Partly refuted. ARP4761 remains unresolved and dangerous, but after the counterexamples the most serious technical threat is meta-diagnosis and structural FDI, which the frontier report ranked lower. The threat ordering changed because the candidate's own centre of gravity moved.
refuted_predictions.why_kept: It shows the prior-art ranking was contingent on a formulation that did not survive.

refuted_predictions.prediction: Predicted at the start of this stage that a source audit would either find no runtime topology change (killing the runtime framing) or find one that mattered.
refuted_predictions.outcome: Neither. The audit found a real runtime topology change AND found that it does not demonstrably matter diagnostically (counterexample A applies to the very pair found) AND found that PX4 already publishes the information. Three outcomes at once, none of them the two predicted.
refuted_predictions.why_kept: The prediction was binary and the result was not.

preserved_prior_verdicts.effective evidence independence as a gra: PROVENANCE_METRIC_INSUFFICIENT - refuted as the central quantity in this stage

what_must_be_true_before_stage_0b: ARP4761 / ARP4761A Common Cause and Common Mode Analysis read in full; the design-time vs runtime question answered in writing.
Le Caillec conditional-independence testing read in full; whether a shared-information verdict is ever attached to a decision.
Meta-diagnosis and structural FDI read in full; whether a formally correct but currently uninformative relation is already in scope.
Noack et al. ICI and the data-incest graph literature read in full.
A quantity other than kappa_prov identified as the primary measurand, since kappa_prov is insufficient and may not be redefined to rescue it.
If any of the above already performs the runtime computation: record the kill and stop.
